name: ActiveState
conference_description: Who Vets AI's Code? Open source software runs the modern software stack. That was true before AI code generators showed up, and while coding has changed, the use of open source hasn't. What's changed is the pace and volume at which open source software enters your environment, and who, or what, is making the call to bring it in. AI coding assistants can suggest and accept dependencies far faster than any manual review process was built to handle. The result is more open source software, arriving faster, with less opportunity for anyone to ask whether it should be trusted in the first place. So the question isn't whether your organization runs on open source software. It's whether anyone, human or AI, is vetting what comes in before it reaches your cluster. The ActiveState Curated Catalog is the answer by giving platform and security teams a single, governed source for open source software, built from source inside SLSA Level 3 infrastructure, with full provenance and remediation on contractual SLAs. When an AI coding tool requests a dependency, it resolves against the catalog instead of an unvetted public registry. Developers keep the workflow and the velocity they already have, and security teams get a governance layer that holds at the point of ingestion, before the dependency ever reaches a build. The result is a software supply chain your security team can actually account for, whether the code behind it was written by a person or generated by an agent. Learn more at http://www.activestate.com.
ai_what_they_do: ActiveState supplies vetted open-source software components, built from source and patched continuously, through a single governed catalog that developers and AI coding assistants pull from instead of public registries.
ai_who_its_for: Platform teams; Security teams; Security leaders and CISOs; Engineering leaders; DevOps and platform engineers; Developers using AI coding assistants; Enterprises in regulated industries
ai_problems_solved: AI coding assistants pull open-source dependencies from public registries with no vetting or provenance; Open-source dependencies arrive faster than security teams can review them; Known vulnerabilities in open-source packages; it says its components have about 95% fewer CVEs than community equivalents; Slow patching of vulnerable components; it promises fixes within 5 business days for critical CVEs and 10 for high; Engineers losing time to triaging and manually patching dependencies; Scanner noise and false positives, which it says VEX data cuts by about 68%; Producing audit-ready provenance and SBOMs for compliance; Dependency conflicts and environment drift

name: empirik
conference_description: Coding agents made writing software autonomous. Running infrastructure is next. Modern infra, spanning Clouds, SaaS, and on-prem, has outgrown human comprehension. Thousands of changes are deployed daily, yet engineers are still forced to manually guess what a change will touch, whether it’s safe, and what broke when an incident occurs. Today, humans are the safety layer. That doesn't scale. Empirik is the AI engineer for enterprise infrastructure. It operates on a deterministic model of the environment, built from Empirik’s continuously compiled graph of resources, relationships, changes and provenance. It understands changes, determines their impact across the environment, and validates decisions before they cause outages, create security or compliance risk, or slow developers down. Engineering teams use Empirik to understand blast radius, prevent outages, detect unauthorized changes, accelerate root cause analysis, and give engineers and coding agents trusted infrastructure context. Over time, Empirik safely executes these decisions itself. What coding agents did for software, Empirik does for infra.

ai_who_its_for: Platform engineering teams; Infrastructure and operations engineers; Engineering teams in large enterprises; Teams using AI coding agents that need infrastructure context
ai_problems_solved: Not knowing the blast radius of an infrastructure change before it is deployed; Outages caused by changes; Slow root cause analysis during incidents; Unauthorised changes made outside the approved path; Drift between intended, deployed and running infrastructure; Non-compliant resources and infrastructure-as-code drift; Orphaned and idle infrastructure that wastes money; Unknown VM dependencies before a migration

name: Vijil
conference_description: Vijil helps developers ship agents that business owners can trust in production. Enterprises are building agents faster than they can govern them: manual security review sets the release timeline, traditional QA doesn't cover prompt injection or hallucination, and untracked prototypes accumulate until an audit finds them. Vijil replaces that with an API-first platform that manages agents throughout their lifecycle — discover, identify, evaluate, harden, monitor, evolve, and attest — all in one place. Vijil Discover scans repositories, cloud infrastructure, and production environments to fingerprint every agent, authorized or shadow, into a centralized registry. Vijil Diamond evaluates agents against hundreds of context-specific scenarios and returns a Trust Score in minutes, not weeks, so evidence of trustworthiness is generated continuously rather than assembled by hand before each release. Vijil is deliberately neutral infrastructure: it works with any open source model, agent development framework, and agent deployment platform, including LangChain, CrewAI, and Agent Development Kit.
ai_what_they_do: Vijil is a platform for finding, testing, guarding and monitoring AI agents across an enterprise, so companies can show their agents are reliable, secure and within policy before and after they go into production.
ai_who_its_for: Agent developers; Chief information security officers and risk owners; Business owners accountable for AI agents; Enterprises deploying AI agents
ai_problems_solved: Manual security review holding up agent releases; Traditional QA not covering prompt injection or hallucination; Untracked shadow agents piling up until an audit finds them; Agents drifting toward easier rewards that break policy; Stopping planted instructions from moving money or data; Showing auditors controls under the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001; Telling whether an agent improved at the job or just at the tests
ai_products: Vijil Discover: Scans code, cloud and production to find every agent and give each a SPIFFE identity in one registry.; Vijil Diamond: Evaluates agents against hundreds of context-specific and adversarial scenarios and returns a Trust Score.; Vijil Dome: Open-source in-agent guards that control what an agent may access, invoke and disclose, with OpenTelemetry metrics.; Vijil Darwin: In development: traces agent failures and proposes improved agents as pull requests within set limits.
